title: Company-wide policies and processes: access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates
author: Ava Chen
body:
Overview:
This document centralizes Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and common internal templates. It is intended for all employees, contractors, and stakeholders who request, approve, or administer company resources.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and third-party vendors with access to Redwood systems or data.
- Covers systems hosted in Redwood, Dedicated, and Private environments where Redwood staff have administrative or operational responsibilities.

Primary owners and escalation contacts:
- Policy owner: People Ops (people-ops@redwood.example)
- Security owner (access, data): Security & Compliance (security@redwood.example)
- Procurement & vendor owner: Finance & Legal (procurement@redwood.example)
- Travel & expenses: Finance (travel@redwood.example)

1) Access & permissions
Principles:
- Least privilege by default; access granted for a defined business purpose and duration.
- Role-based access control (RBAC) where supported; groups preferred over individual grants.
- All privileged access requires approval and justifiable business rationale.
- Periodic access reviews and audit logging enabled for all sensitive systems.

Onboarding / Offboarding process:
1. New-hire access request via Access Request template (link: /confluence/access-request-template).
2. Hiring manager selects predefined role profile; People Ops and Security perform approvals.
3. Access is provisioned with documented TTL (default 90 days for non-critical roles).
4. Offboarding checklist executed within 4 business hours of termination: disable accounts, revoke tokens, reclaim hardware.

Privileged access & emergency (break-glass):
- Privileged (admin/root) access is limited to designated engineers and must be requested with justification and a time-bound window.
- Emergency access requires post-facto approval and an incident ticket documenting the action.

Access reviews and attestations:
- Quarterly access reviews for all systems classified as Confidential or Regulated.
- Team leads must attest to the necessity of each granted permission; audit evidence retained for 3 years.

2) Change management
Change categories:
- Standard (pre-approved, low-risk): routine config changes that follow a runbook.
- Normal (scheduled, requires approval): feature releases or infra changes that require approval from the change approver and a change owner.
- Emergency (immediate): outages or security fixes; must be documented and reviewed in post-change review.

Process:
1. Submit Change Request via change-request template (link: /confluence/change-request). Include owner, rollback plan, SLO impact analysis, and test plan.
2. Normal changes reviewed by the Change Advisory Board (CAB) weekly; CAB members = infra, SRE, security, product.
3. Scheduled maintenance windows: Saturdays 02:00–06:00 UTC (monthly) for disruptive infra changes.
4. Rollback and verification steps required for all Normal and Emergency changes.

Approval thresholds and windows:
- Changes that affect production SLOs or customer-facing latency >5% require sign-off from SRE lead and Product owner.
- Freeze windows: last 5 business days of each quarter and during major launches.

3) Data management
Data classification:
- PUBLIC: intended for public distribution.
- INTERNAL: use within Redwood, low confidentiality.
- CONFIDENTIAL: contains PII, business-sensitive material.
- REGULATED: subject to legal/regulatory controls (e.g., customer PHI, PCI data).

Handling rules:
- Encryption: Data at rest and in transit must use approved encryption (TLS 1.2+ for transit, AES-256 or equivalent at rest).
- Access: Confidential and Regulated data access requires role-based approval and data processing agreement where applicable.
- Storage: Regulated data must only be stored in designated regions and audited storage buckets.

Retention and deletion:
- Retention policies defined per data class and business need. Default retention: Public (no retention), Internal (2 years), Confidential (7 years or business need), Regulated (as required by law).
- Data deletion requests follow the Data Deletion Request template and must be approved by Data Steward.

Backups and disaster recovery:
- Critical datasets have daily backups with retention consistent with the retention policy.
- Recovery point objective (RPO) targets and recovery time objective (RTO) documented per service in service-level runbooks.

Data sharing and third parties:
- Data sharing with third parties requires a Data Processing Agreement (DPA) and security review.
- Export controls: follow the SecureSDLC and legal guidance for cross-border transfers.

4) Procurement & expenses
Procurement workflow:
- Purchases under $5,000: manager approval required.
- Purchases $5,000–$50,000: department head + Finance approval.
- Purchases >$50,000: VP-level approval and Finance + Legal review; competitive bidding recommended.
- Use Purchase Order (PO) for vendor engagements >$10,000 where possible.

Corporate cards and expenses:
- Corporate card holders must complete expense training annually.
- Expense submission timeline: within 30 days of transaction. Exceptions must be documented.
- Receipts required for all expenses >$25. Airfare and lodging require itemized receipts.

Expense policy highlights:
- Meals: up to $75 per person for client-facing meals; internal team dinners require manager pre-approval if >$50 per person.
- Ground transportation: rideshare and taxi reasonable; mileage reimbursed at company rate.
- Subscription renewals: renewal notice to procurement 60 days before expiration.

5) Vendor management
Vendor selection and onboarding:
- Vendor intake form required for all new vendor relationships (link: /confluence/vendor-intake).
- Risk assessment: Security, Privacy, Financial, and Compliance reviews conducted for vendors with access to Confidential/Regulated data.
- Contract requirements: security SLA, breach notification timelines, data return/deletion clauses, indemnities as appropriate.

Ongoing vendor oversight:
- Annual security questionnaire or SOC2 report required for vendors handling Confidential or Regulated data.
- Vendor performance reviews: quarterly for strategic vendors, annually for tactical vendors.
- Contract renewal: begin negotiation 90 days prior to contract end.

Termination:
- Offboarding checklist includes revocation of access, retrieval of assets, and verification of data deletion or return.

6) Travel policy
Booking & approvals:
- Domestic travel: manager approval required. International travel: manager + People Ops approval.
- Use approved travel booking tools where available; exceptions require pre-approval.

Cost guidelines:
- Economy class for flights <6 hours; Premium Economy for flights 6–12 hours with People Ops approval for exceptions.
- Per diem: see Travel Per Diem template (link: /confluence/travel-per-diem).
- Lodging: standard business hotels; nightly limit varies by city (refer to city matrix in Travel Per Diem template).

Safety & emergency:
- Emergency contact: travel@redwood.example. People Ops will assist with evacuation and emergency support.
- Passport & visa: traveler responsible for ensuring valid travel documents; company will reimburse visa fees with receipts.

7) Internal templates and links
Common templates (use internal Confluence templates):
- Access Request: /confluence/access-request-template
- Change Request: /confluence/change-request
- Data Deletion Request: /confluence/data-deletion-request
- Vendor Intake: /confluence/vendor-intake
- PO Request: /confluence/po-request
- Expense Report: /confluence/expense-report-template
- Travel Per Diem & City Matrix: /confluence/travel-per-diem

Governance, exceptions, and updates:
- Exceptions: must be documented and approved by the policy owner and Security/Finance as appropriate; exceptions recorded in the policy exceptions register.
- Policy review cadence: Annual review led by People Ops; ad-hoc updates for regulatory or operational changes.
- Enforcement: Violations may result in access revocation, disciplinary action, or contractual remedies for vendors.
